root_cause: The Tab keydown event on the datepicker input has defaultPrevented set to true, likely due to a vanilla-calendar-pro (VCP) keydown listener that calls preventDefault() on Tab key. This blocks the browser's default focus navigation to the next form field.
repair_strategy: Add a capture-phase keydown listener on the datepicker input that calls stopImmediatePropagation() on Tab key to prevent VCP's listener from running, then hides the calendar. This allows the browser's default focus move to proceed while closing the datepicker popup.

constructor(element?: string | Element | null, config?: Partial<DatepickerConfig> | null) {
    super(element, config)

    this._calendar = null
    this._isShown = false
    this._onTabKeyDownCapture = null

    this._initCalendar()
  }

expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key navigation from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field as expected. The datepicker popup closes when tabbing out, maintaining a predictable keyboard interface.
functional_risks: Capture-phase listener might interfere with other capture-phase listeners (unlikely in this codebase).
stopImmediatePropagation prevents all other keydown listeners on the input for Tab key, but the calendar doesn't use Tab internally.
Direct addEventListener usage bypasses EventHandler, but is necessary for capture phase.
verification_requirements: Verify Tab from departure date moves focus to passengers field.
Verify datepicker calendar closes when tabbing out.
Verify Tab works when datepicker not open.
Verify date selection via mouse/keyboard in calendar works.
